parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering task and the need to infer fselect behavior only by running the provided binary and reading bundled docs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent built shared fixtures, then chose a foreground ten-child AgentSwarm where each child owned a behavioral spec area; implementation was assigned to the parent only after the swarm phase.
parallel.implementation: No replacement implementation was written. The completed work was documentation: specs for traversal, dates, output formats, and group/order/subqueries.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered archive retained README/docs/licenses/original executable and added mkfixtures.sh plus four spec files, but no compile.sh or replacement source tree.
parallel.verification: Children performed many black-box probes and wrote exact behavioral findings, but there was no integrated verification of a new executable because no implementation existed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Six feature-spec children were cancelled, no implementation began, artifact validation failed, and the official evaluator reported compile_failed with all tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering constraints and selected an original Python implementation strategy rather than wrapping the binary.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent used a todo list covering probing, language choice, parser, file search, functions, output formats, interactive mode, and differential tests.
serial.implementation: After extensive probing it started a Python codebase, writing src/fselect/rustfmt.py and src/fselect/dates.py and planning additional modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final archive included src/fselect/dates.py, helptext.py, rustfmt.py, docs, licenses, and the original executable, but not enough assembled build or entry-point structure to compile.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran many behavioral probes against the binary but did not reach integrated differential testing of a finished replacement executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation stopped after a few modules, compile failed, and the official evaluator reported all 3435 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel acknowledged the benchmark requirement to write an original behavioral reimplementation and supplied clean-room rules to every probing child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial acknowledged the same requirement and explicitly planned a Python executable rather than a source lookup or binary wrapper.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the required behavior space; the difference was not a requirements misunderstanding but how each converted discovery into implementation work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by feature-area probes, assigning ten children to write specs while the parent planned to implement only after foreground swarm completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership in one agent with an end-to-end todo list from probing through parser/search/functions/output and differential tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's ownership plan made investigation the entire first phase; serial retained implementation ownership throughout and reached code writing before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children received common rules, docs, binary path, fixture path, and distinct spec-file targets; no component interface contract was needed because no implementation components were delegated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated findings in one context and translated them into a planned set of Python modules with clear internal responsibilities.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced child reports rather than interfaces between implementation components; serial created an internal implementation plan from its probe context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not write replacement source; status artifacts show only mkfixtures.sh, four specs, docs, licenses, git metadata, and the original executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial began the replacement implementation by writing Python modules for value formatting and date parsing under src/fselect.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial advanced into source creation, while parallel stopped at behavioral documentation and never created the implementation files needed for a build.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The swarm returned only at cancellation with four completed spec reports and six aborted children, with a resume hint but no later parent action.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its local probe findings directly informed the implementation modules it started writing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's results arrived as a partial swarm aggregate at closure, while serial's findings remained in the same actor and were acted on before cancellation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate spec files in the shared workspace; shared todo-state clobbering was observed, but no implementation merge or file overwrite was completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a single-agent source tree with no subagent/shared-write conflicts, but it also did not finish executable assembly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel avoided source merge conflicts because it produced no source components; serial had coherent partial modules but no complete assembled deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children verified observed behaviors through probes, but no new executable existed for whole-task acceptance testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran many probes and intended differential tests, but cancellation occurred before a finished implementation could be tested end to end.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked final integrated acceptance; parallel's verification stayed at behavioral research, while serial's was preparatory to an unfinished implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run window in the foreground swarm and closed on cancellation with six aborted children and no implementation pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after extensive local probing and only two module writes, leaving the build incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the budget, but parallel spent that budget before implementation began, whereas serial spent it after beginning a partial implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false with compile_failed and 3435 tests not run. The trajectories still differ materially because the parallel run delivered only exploration specs after a foreground swarm, while the serial run began an incomplete Python implementation.
parallel_contributors: Foreground ten-child exploration swarm deferred implementation until after child results; the run closed with only four completed specs and six aborted children.
The submitted parallel artifact contained no replacement source or compile path, only specs and original workspace files.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one implementation owner and wrote src/fselect modules after probing.
Serial still failed because implementation and assembly were incomplete at timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial made ordinary implementation progress in Python modules but did not finish parser/search/output modules or packaging.
Parallel did not expose ordinary coding defects because it did not reach implementation.

retained_patterns.reason: Parallel used its child mechanism for a broad investigation wave and explicitly waited for that wave before implementation. The wave reached cancellation with six aborted children, leaving no new implementation in the delivered artifact, while serial had started source modules before its own timeout.
